candidates.exact_span: If requirements for sludge management practices or pollutant criteria become more stringent than the sludge pollutant limits or acceptable management practices in this permit, or control a pollutant not listed in this permit, this permit may be modified or revoked and reissued to conform to the requirements promulgated at Section 405(d)(2) of the Clean Water Act.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether more stringent Section 405(d)(2) pollutant criteria supersede or supplement the permit's listed limits affects which numeric limits are enforceable for compliance comparison during FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: If new limits for Molybdenum are promulgated prior to permit expiration, then those limits shall become directly enforceable.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether Molybdenum limits are directly enforceable for exceedance analysis depends on whether new limits were promulgated before permit expiration within the evaluation period.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be tested once during the life of the permit within one year from the effective date of the permit in accordance with the method specified at 40 CFR 268, Appendix I (Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP)) or other approved methods.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether TCLP testing was required during FY2025 depends on permit effective date, the one-time timing window, and whether an approved alternative method was used.

candidates.exact_span: Sludge shall be tested after final treatment prior to leaving the POTW site.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The point at which the TCLP obligation attaches (after final treatment, before leaving site) affects whether monitoring was required for a given sludge batch or reporting period.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge determined to be a hazardous waste in accordance with 40 CFR Part 261, shall be handled according to RCRA standards for the disposal of hazardous waste in accordance with 40 CFR Part 262.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A hazardous-waste determination shifts applicable monitoring and reporting from land-application pollutant testing to RCRA disposal requirements, changing what monitoring was required and how missing or non-numeric results should be classified.

candidates.exact_span: The disposal of sewage sludge determined to be a hazardous waste, in other than a certified hazardous waste disposal facility shall be prohibited.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether sludge is classified as hazardous waste changes which enforceable disposal constraints apply and whether land-application pollutant limits remain the operative compliance basis.

candidates.exact_span: The Information Management Section, telephone no. (214) 665-6750, and the appropriate state agency shall be notified of test failure within 24 hours.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether notification monitoring/reporting was required depends on whether a TCLP test failure occurred and whether the 24-hour notification obligation was triggered.

candidates.exact_span: A written rep ort shall be provided to this office within 7 days after failing the TCLP.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a written report was required during FY2025 depends on whether a TCLP failure occurred and how the 7-day deadline is measured.

candidates.exact_span: The report will contain test results, certification that unauthorized disposal has not occurred and a summary of alternative disposal plans that comply with RCRA standards for the disposal of hazardous waste.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The required report contents establish what evidence must exist after a TCLP failure; absent those elements, whether monitoring/reporting obligations were met or evidence is missing remains unresolved.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall not be applied to the land if the concentration of the pollutants exceeds the pollutant concentration criteria in Table 1.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This provision sets an enforceable numeric land-application limit tied to Table 1 pollutant criteria; interpretation of which pollutants and concentrations apply determines exceedance analysis.

candidates.exact_span: The frequency of testing for pollutants in Table 1 is found in Element 1, Section I.C.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Monitoring obligation timing for Table 1 pollutants is delegated to Section I.C; without resolving that cross-reference, whether testing was required in a given FY2025 period remains indeterminate.
